title: penny-jar tenant saver: automated slab defaults and soft-quant fallbacks
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: tenants with bursty traffic and conservative defaults often burn budget during cold windows because prefill and quantization defaults are not tailored. This PR introduces the 'penny-jar' tenant saver: an orchestrator that generates safe slab-prefill defaults, a soft-quant fallback path, and a simple CLI for operators to preview and apply tenant-scoped suggestions. Implementation summary: added pkg/econ/pennyjar orchestrator implementing heatmap-driven slab sizing, sample-weighted prefill thresholds, unit-econ estimation (uCost per 1k tokens) and quality delta tracking hooks; introduced a soft-quant fallback in the serving runtime that can switch to a compatible lower-precision quant profile at variant boundaries with a configurable decay window; added cmd/pennyjarctl for dry-run previews, tenant-scoped apply, and a --simulate flag that runs a local cost/latency/quality projection; exposed telemetry: pennies.uCost, pennies.quality_delta, pennies.applied_tenants; added unit/integration tests and an e2e smoke test showing a 12-18% median token cost reduction on synthetic shopper workload. Safety & rollout: all suggestions are opt-in by default and behind a feature flag. The orchestrator emits a suggested config rather than auto-applying; when applied the system runs a shadow canary (5% traffic) and evaluates quality signals over the configured sample set; automatic rollback triggers if quality_delta > 0.5 (system-default) or if latency SLO degradation > 10%. Backwards compatibility: changes are additive and gated; default serving paths unchanged until explicit apply. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration smoke, [x] CLI help and man page, [x] docs/ops guide, [x] telemetry dashboard panels, [x] e2e smoke pass. Related: See ENG-2245 for heuristic design and PM-1022 for product acceptance criteria. Risks: quantized fallbacks can introduce subtle quality drift; mitigations include sample-based validation, canary windows, conservative default thresholds, and an immediate failover path to the pinned model variant. Deployment notes: helm values include pennyjar.enabled=false by default. CI: unit-tests: pass, integration-smoke: pass, linters: pass, e2e: pass after 1 flaky retry. Merge: squash and merge; post-merge follow-up to add tenant onboarding playbook.

review_comments: Marco Li: Nice end-to-end but the default rollback threshold seems aggressive; suggest 0.5->0.75 for initial rollout. Author (Aisha): raised to 0.75 by default and added a config knob.
Jordan Patel: Can we avoid cross-tenant cache pollution during shadow canary? Author (Aisha): added tenant-scoped cache namespaces and a test in tests/unit to validate isolation.
Sofia Nguyen: CLI UX nit: preview output should include estimated 95th percentile latency impact. Author (Aisha): added P95 estimates and updated docs and CLI help.
merge_commit_summary: squash: penny-jar tenant saver: orchestrator, soft-quant fallback, pennyjarctl CLI, telemetry, docs
release_notes: Add penny-jar tenant saver (feature-flagged) that suggests tenant prefills and offers a safe soft-quant fallback path to reduce per-token cost. Includes pennyjarctl for dry-run previews and an ops rollout playbook. Opt-in; feature disabled by default.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: quality regressions from quantization fallbacks. Mitigations: conservative default thresholds, shadow canary windows, sample-based evals, immediate failover to pinned variant, and metric-driven automatic rollback. Added extra unit/integration tests and telemetry to detect regressions quickly.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (disabled) -> Stage 1 (dry-run suggestions only) -> Stage 2 (canary 5% shadow and simulated apply) -> Stage 3 (canary 25%) -> Stage 4 (50%) -> Stage 5 (100%). Automatic rollback triggers on quality_delta > configured default (0.75) or latency SLO degradation > 10%. Ops can abort via feature flag flip or pennyjarctl revert.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on safety boundaries in pkg/serving/quant_fallback.go and the tenant cache isolation changes. The orchestrator heuristics live behind a feature flag; most logic is covered by unit tests and a synthetic e2e scenario included in tests/e2e.
